title: Sr. Engineer - Mechanical (Lifting)
description: Job Purpose To plan, engineer, supervise, and ensure the safe execution of all lifting and hoisting operations at project sites in compliance with project specifications, local regulations, and international lifting standards. Key Responsibilities Prepare and review lifting plans, method statements, risk assessments, and lift studies for routine and critical lifting operations. Conduct engineering calculations for crane selection, load distribution, lifting capacity, ground bearing pressure, and rigging requirements. Verify lifting equipment certifications, inspection records, and compliance with applicable standards. Coordinate with site construction, EHS, logistics, and subcontractor teams to ensure safe execution of lifting activities. Supervise critical lifting operations and provide technical guidance to crane operators, riggers, and lifting supervisors. Ensure compliance with project HSE requirements, OSHA standards, BS 7121, LOLER, and local authority regulations.

title: Senior Site Project Engineer - Habshan
description: The Role This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced Senior Project Engineer with a proven track record in leading and managing multi-disciplinary teams, ensuring the successful execution of projects and alignment with company goals for a high-profile client. Our Clients and Projects Designing the future. Transforming the world. Wood's Oil, Gas & New Energies business is built on a strong legacy of delivering large and complex projects for national and international energy companies across the globe. You, our enabling teams, are at the very forefront of transformative projects that are providing sustainable power to generations to come. We are the ones to bring low-carbon concepts to reality. The role ensures effective integration of engineering, procurement, construction, quality, HSE, project controls and commissioning activities to achieve project objectives in accordance with approved scope, schedule, budget, technical specifications and contractual requirements. Working under the direction of the Lead Project Engineer and Project Manager, the Senior Project Engineer serves as a key focal point for multidisciplinary engineering coordination, technical issue resolution, deliverables management and interface control. The position ensures that engineering outputs are delivered in a timely manner, technical queries are resolved efficiently, and design solutions meet project requirements while supporting safe, efficient and constructible site execution. Wood is a global leader in consulting, engineering and operations for the energy and materials sectors. With 33,000 people in around 50 countries, Wood supports clients across the full asset lifecycle, delivering safe, predictable outcomes while enabling resilient operations and a lower carbon future. Wood forms the Energy & Materials pillar of Sidara - a global partnership uniting leading multidisciplinary engineering, design, and project management companies. www.woodgroup.com Diversity Statement We are an equal opportunity employer that recognises the value of a diverse workforce. All suitably qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment on the basis of objective criteria and without regard to the following (which is a non-exhaustive list): race, colour, age, religion, gender, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, protected veteran status, or other characteristics in accordance with the relevant governing laws. Responsibilities: Coordinate day-to-day engineering and technical activities across multiple disciplines to ensure alignment with project requirements, approved design criteria, engineering specifications, contractual obligations and ADNOC Gas standards. Support the Lead Project Engineer in implementing the engineering execution plan, managing deliverables, monitoring engineering progress and ensuring that technical activities remain aligned with the overall project schedule and execution strategy. Coordinate with discipline engineers, engineering leads, procurement, construction, planning, project controls, quality, HSE, commissioning and document control teams to facilitate timely completion of project activities. Monitor engineering deliverables against approved schedules, identify outstanding documents and technical dependencies, and follow up with responsible discipline teams to ensure timely submission, review, approval and release. Maintain engineering registers, technical query logs, interface registers, action trackers, engineering deliverables lists and other project records to provide accurate visibility of engineering status and outstanding issues. Undertake frequent site visits to Habshan to coordinate with construction personnel, inspect field conditions, review construction progress, identify engineering constraints and facilitate timely resolution of technical issues affecting site execution. Act as a key liaison between site-based construction teams and office-based engineering disciplines, ensuring that field observations, technical queries, design discrepancies and construction feedback are communicated clearly and addressed within agreed timelines. Coordinate and expedite the resolution of requests for information, technical queries, field change requests, design clarifications, technical deviations and engineering-related non-conformance reports in accordance with established project procedures. Review engineering drawings, specifications, calculations, technical documents and design deliverables for completeness, consistency and coordination, escalating technical issues to the relevant discipline leads and Lead Project Engineer. Ensure that engineering deliverables are developed and issued in accordance with approved project specifications, applicable international codes and standards, ADNOC requirements, quality procedures and document control protocols. Coordinate multidisciplinary engineering interfaces across process, mechanical, piping, civil, structural, electrical, instrumentation, control systems, telecom, fire and gas, HVAC and other applicable disciplines. Facilitate interdisciplinary design reviews, technical coordination meetings, constructability reviews and engineering workshops to identify design conflicts, interface gaps, installation constraints and potential construction risks. Support the coordination of engineering inputs required for procurement activities, including technical requisitions, vendor documentation, technical clarifications, material specifications and equipment data, ensuring timely resolution of outstanding matters. Follow up on vendor engineering documentation, review status, technical comments and approval cycles in coordination with discipline engineers and procurement personnel to avoid impacts on procurement, fabrication, delivery and installation schedules. Coordinate with construction teams to ensure that approved drawings, specifications, material requirements and technical instructions are available ahead of planned site activities. Identify engineering-related constraints affecting construction work fronts, including incomplete design information, material discrepancies, access limitations, technical approvals and unresolved interfaces, and coordinate corrective actions with the responsible teams. Support the preparation, review and implementation of engineering schedules, look-ahead plans, deliverables forecasts and priority lists in line with construction sequencing and project milestones. Monitor engineering progress and report deviations from planned targets, highlighting potential impacts on construction, procurement, cost, quality and schedule to the Lead Project Engineer and Project Manager. Coordinate with planning and project controls personnel to assess the impact of engineering delays, technical changes, outstanding approvals and design revisions on the overall project programme. Assist in the management of engineering changes by coordinating technical assessments, obtaining discipline inputs, documenting the rationale for proposed changes and evaluating potential impacts on scope, cost, schedule, quality, procurement and construction. Support the maintenance of project risk registers and interface registers by identifying technical risks, recording constraints, tracking mitigation measures and escalating issues requiring management intervention. Coordinate brownfield engineering activities, where applicable, including existing facility surveys, site verification, tie-in interfaces, design modifications and technical coordination with operations and construction teams. Support engineering coordination for construction activities within or adjacent to operating gas processing facilities, ensuring that technical solutions account for operational constraints, safety requirements and applicable permit-to-work and SIMOPS arrangements. Work closely with HSE and process safety teams to ensure that engineering activities address identified hazards, design risks, safety study recommendations and relevant operational integrity requirements. Ensure engineering-related quality issues are documented, communicated and resolved through the approved quality management system, including appropriate closure of technical comments, non-conformances and corrective actions. Coordinate the preparation and closure of engineering actions arising from project meetings, technical reviews, site inspections, design reviews, client comments and construction coordination sessions. Participate in project progress meetings, engineering coordination meetings, construction interface meetings, vendor meetings and client reviews, providing accurate updates on engineering status, outstanding actions, risks and required decisions. Prepare engineering status reports, technical summaries, action trackers, deliverables forecasts and other project documentation required by the Lead Project Engineer, Engineering Manager and Project Manager. Support the implementation of project document control requirements, ensuring that drawings, specifications, technical correspondence and engineering deliverables are appropriately reviewed, approved, distributed and maintained at the correct revision. Coordinate with commissioning and system completion teams to ensure that engineering documentation, technical clarifications, system information and outstanding design actions are addressed in support of pre-commissioning, commissioning and start-up. Support the preparation and completion of as-built documentation, engineering handover records, technical dossiers, vendor documentation and other required deliverables for final project handover to ADNOC Gas. Promote effective communication, teamwork and accountability among engineering disciplines and project stakeholders, ensuring that technical issues are addressed proactively and that commitments are followed through to completion. Identify opportunities for design optimization, value engineering, standardization and improved engineering coordination while maintaining compliance with approved technical requirements and safety standards. Ensure that lessons learned, recurring technical issues and site feedback are captured and communicated to the relevant engineering teams to prevent rework and improve project performance. Perform other duties within the scope of the position as required to support the safe, timely and successful delivery of the project. Qualifications: Skills And Qualifications What makes you remarkable? At Wood, we are committed to equal opportunities and welcome all talented individuals to consider joining our team. So even if you don't match every statement below but feel you have some of the experience, knowledge or skills needed for this role, we encourage you to apply. Minimum 12 to 15 years of experience in the Oil & Gas industry. Proven experience in ADNOC Gas projects. Thorough knowledge and practical application of DGS, AGES, and AGPS standards. Strong background in Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) projects. Extensive site construction experience in operating Oil & Gas facilities. Experience in Gas Processing Plants and shutdown/turnaround execution. Hands-on experience in brownfield modification projects, including work within live operating facilities. Proven experience in planning and execution of large-diameter piping tie-ins. Experience in heavy lifting and installation of large vessels and static equipment. Ability to coordinate multidiscipline activities involving engineering, construction, commissioning, and operations teams. Familiarity with permit-to-work systems, SIMOPS, HSE requirements, and shutdown planning. Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.

title: Cloud Architect
description: Who We Are At Kyndryl, we run and reimagine the mission-critical technology systems that drive advantage for the world’s leading businesses. We are at the heart of progress; with proven expertise and a continuous flow of AI-powered insight, enabling smarter decisions, faster innovation, and a lasting competitive edge. For our people—Kyndryls—that means doing purposeful work that powers human progress. Join us and experience a flexible, supportive environment where your well-being is prioritized and your potential can thrive. The Role Infrastructure Architects are the key link between Kyndryl and our clients. You’re in a technical leadership role, uniting and guiding stakeholders from clients, governance, and project executives to delivery and sometimes even the vendors who work with the client. You’ll be there from the start of a project — understanding what’s needed and figuring out the best technical solution. And you’ll be there at the finish, delivering the right product on time and within budget. As an Infrastructure Architect, you’ll draw upon the full breadth of your talent and experience. This is a technical leadership role, so we want you to bring your vision, knowledge, and leadership to each project. To the client, you’re the subject matter expert – consulting early, gathering inputs, understanding what they need from our solution. You define what Kyndryl can do to meet this solution. You design the best solution for the job. And finally, you’re the tech leader for implementation. Responsibilities Architecture & Migration Leadership: Lead architecture workshops and design scalable GCP cloud solutions, including workload migration strategies from on-premises data centers to the cloud. Infrastructure as Code (IaC) & Automation: Build and deliver automated infrastructure, platform deployments, and configuration workflows using tools like Terraform, Ansible, Deployment Manager, and GitOps. CI/CD & DevSecOps Implementation: Design and set up secure, automated CI/CD pipelines leveraging both GCP native services (Cloud Build) and traditional DevOps tools (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Argo, SonarQube). Optimization & Review: Perform periodic architecture reviews to enhance application performance, drive cost optimization, and build internal utilities for safer, high-speed engineering operations. Documentation & Governance: Document technical frameworks and architecture workflows while implementing robust monitoring, SRE practices, and configuration management (e.g., Anthos, GCVE). At Kyndryl we support all major cloud platforms, so you’ll get the chance to use everything you know – and then some. You’ll also become expert at knowing when and how to call on other SMEs outside your wheelhouse. Thinking your way around pre-existing limitations will grow your creativity and flexibility. You’ll learn a lot here, and if you want to work toward certifications there are plenty of opportunities.The rewards for all this are many. You’ll get to influence, create, and deliver something from start to finish. You will have the power to delight our clients. Your future at Kyndryl This role opens the door to many career paths, both vertical and horizontal, and there may be opportunity to travel. It’s a great chance for database administrators or other techs to break into the cloud. It’s also a solid path to become enterprise or chief architect or a distinguished engineer! Whatever you see for yourself, you’ll find the opportunity here. Who You Are You’re good at what you do and possess the required experience to prove it. However, equally as important – you have a growth mindset; keen to drive your own personal and professional development. You are customer-focused – someone who prioritizes customer success in their work. And finally, you’re open and borderless – naturally inclusive in how you work with others. Required Technical and Professional Experience Cloud Architecture (GCP/AWS): Hands-on experience designing multi-tier, fault-tolerant, cloud-native enterprise applications, primarily using GCP and secondarily AWS. Data Center & Infrastructure: Solid understanding of systems, storage, security, and networking across both traditional data center environments and public cloud (IaaS/PaaS). Infrastructure as Code & Automation: Experience automating infrastructure and configurations using tools like Terraform, Ansible, Chef, Puppet, and GitHub. CI/CD & Scripting: Expertise building re-usable release pipelines in Jenkins or AWS CodePipeline, paired with strong scripting skills (Python, Shell/Bash, PowerShell, YAML). OS & Core Tech: Hands-on mastery of both Linux and Windows environments, including database and application interoperability. Preferred Technical and Professional Experience DevSecOps & CI/CD Leadership: Experience leading DevSecOps/SRE projects, setting up GitOps workflows, and designing robust CI/CD pipelines integrating tools like Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Argo, and ELK. title: Principal DevOps Platform Engineer - AWS
description: TechGrove is the Centre of Excellence for Banyan Software, based in Chennai, India. It plays a key role in supporting Banyan's global businesses through technology, security, and software development. TechGrove brings together India's deep pool of technical talent with Banyan's long-term approach to growth, creating a trusted, developer-focused environment where people can do their best work. About the role star/trac builds flow, a logistics platform for yards, gates and loading docks. It handles truck check-in, self- service terminals (kiosks), slot and dock planning, and real-time monitoring for industrial customers. We are moving flow from a single-tenant setup (WildFly, Oracle, one AWS account per customer, Elastic Beanstalk) to a cloud-native, multi-tenant platform: flow6, a multi-tenant flow API (Spring Boot, JDK 21) that serves many customers from one deployment, with strict tenant isolation flow-dynamic-ui, a configuration-driven frontend where pages, queries and forms are data, not code flow-terminal-service, the backend and configurator for our check-in kiosks An analytics and real-time layer: CDC from Postgres and Oracle into Apache Doris, Kafka (MSK), and live push to the UI much of our engineering runs through AI agents in Claude Code. Each agent has a written contract, hard rules and its own tools. Our infrastructure agents are DiVa, who works inside a workload account (EKS clusters, Dockerfiles, CI, GitOps deploys, image scans), and Otto, who works across the AWS Organization (accounts, SSO, shared networking, guardrails). They already do real work. They need a human principal who owns them. This role is that owner. You will run our platform end to end and set up what is still missing, with the agents doing much of the hands-on work under your direction. You will also keep making the agents better: safer, more capable, and more useful to the rest of the team. What you will do Own the platform Run our AWS estate: an AWS Organization with shared Networking, Monitoring and Shared Services accounts, plus customer workload accounts. EKS clusters (one per customer and environment, services as namespaces), ECR, RDS, MSK, Route 53. Own the deploy path end to end: GitLab CI from one standard template, then image build and scan, then a GitOps repo, then ArgoCD on EKS. Take new services to QA and then to production. Today that means flow6-mt, flow-dynamic-ui, the auth service and Keycloak. Make flow6 safe to run as several pods behind one service: per-tenant Quartz schedulers, database locking, cache invalidation across pods, and health and readiness probes. Set up what is missing Production secrets: External Secrets Operator with SSM Parameter Store and pod-level IAM roles (IRSA / Pod Identity), in place of hand-made Kubernetes Secrets. Identity: Keycloak for staff, the existing auth service for customers, and service accounts for system-to- system calls. Observability across accounts with Grafana, Prometheus and Loki. Alarms that are tuned, not noisy. The data platform: Apache Doris, CDC pipelines (Postgres logical replication, Oracle LogMiner), Kafka. Repeatable customer onboarding: account, SSO, VPC, monitoring. Cost governance and a clear view of what runs where and what it costs. Lead the infrastructure agents Own DiVa's and Otto's contracts: their scope, hard rules, process steps and handoffs to the other agents. Turn repeated manual work into skills: small, deterministic Python tools with read-only doctor / list / plan verbs and gated mutating verbs. Examples are Helm releases, kubectl apply, registry cleanup, and an AWS Organization skill. Keep and strengthen the safety rails: agents never delete, every change needs an up-front confirm that states cost and blast radius, guard hooks block destructive commands, and nothing goes to main without review. Check that agent output is correct. Read what they produce, test it against real systems, and fix the contract when an agent is wrong. Record decisions as Target Architecture Decisions (TADs) and keep the shared memory accurate and sourced. Be the principal Make infrastructure decisions on your own and write them down so others can follow. Work with the architects, backend and frontend developers, QA, and our Cloud Ops lead, who runs the existing customer environments. Mentor colleagues who are new to Kubernetes or to working with agents. What you bring Senior to principal-level experience in DevOps, SRE or platform engineering, including running production systems. AWS in depth: EKS, IAM (including cross-account roles and SSO / Identity Center), VPC design (including shared VPCs, RAM, peering and endpoints), ECR, RDS, Secrets Manager / SSM. Kubernetes in production: Helm or Kustomize, GitOps with ArgoCD, add-ons, network setup, rolling deploys. CI/CD: GitLab CI preferred, including self-hosted runners. Container builds with multi-stage Dockerfiles, BuildKit and image scanning (Amazon Inspector). The JVM in containers: Spring Boot services, Gradle / Maven builds, Artifactory. Databases from an operator's view: Postgres and Oracle; connection pools, migrations (Liquibase), password rotation. Scripting: Python and Bash, written to be clear, repeatable and safe. Hands-on work with AI coding agents (Claude Code or similar), or a strong wish to start. You treat an agent as a capable colleague whose work you check, not as a black box. Safety by default: least privilege, no secrets in repos or images, confirm before you mutate, and an understanding of what an SCP or a delete can break. Clear written English. German is a strong plus: many of our customers and colleagues work in German. Nice to have Multi-tenant SaaS platforms: tenant isolation, per-tenant data sources, "no tenant, no service" designs. Kafka / MSK, Apache Doris or another OLAP engine, Debezium or other CDC tooling. Keycloak and OAuth2 / OIDC. Grafana, Prometheus and Loki across several AWS accounts. Moving legacy Java EE (WildFly) workloads to containers. Proxmox / LXC or other on-prem CI infrastructure. Writing prompts, agent contracts, or evaluation suites for LLM agents. Your first 90 days 1. Weeks 1–4: Learn the estate and the agents. Run DiVa and Otto on real tasks. Write down where their contracts are thin or wrong, and fix the first gaps. 2. Weeks 5–8: Finish the QA rollout of the new stack (flow6-mt, flow-dynamic-ui, auth service, Keycloak hardening). Put production secrets handling (ESO + SSM + IRSA) in place. 3. Weeks 9–12: Agree a production readiness plan for multi-pod flow6 and the first production cluster with the team. Ship at least one new DiVa skill that removes a manual step from that path. Apple Services Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) teams are responsible for the systems and services that directly support those customers and their experiences. We are looking for an SRE with experience in building and supporting highly available customer-facing services. You will apply SRE best practices to ensure our systems and services' availability, reliability, and performance. Operate, monitor, and triage all aspects of our production and non-production environments. Collaborate with other engineers on code, infrastructure, design reviews, and process enhancements. Minimum Qualifications 6+ years of demonstrated expertise in Site Reliability Engineering, Infrastructure Ops or DevOps-focused role. Understanding of SRE principles, includes monitoring, alerting, error budgets, fault analysis, capacity planning, automation and toil reduction. Proficiency in at least one programming language - Python, Go or Java. Experience managing and scaling distributed systems in a public, private, or hybrid cloud environment. Experience with microservices architecture and container orchestration using Kubernetes or similar technologies. Preferred Qualifications BS or MS in Computer Science / related fields or equivalent work experience. Experience running Tier 1 services for 24/7 support. Strong understanding of Linux operating system fundamentals, networking principles, and system management. Strong sense of ownership, with a desire to communicate and collaborate with other engineers and teams. At Apple, we believe accessibility is a fundamental human right. description: Summary Do you want to help build some of the largest and most consequential enterprise and customer technology systems in the world? Join Apple’s Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization. IS&T is the engine behind everything Apple does for customers and for the people who build for them. It’s Apple’s central nervous system. Supporting 2.5 billion active Apple devices, processing billions of secure transactions, and keeping the technology that defines modern life running flawlessly, IS&T makes the impossible feel effortless.” Do you love building solutions to handle global complexity and immense scale? The team connects the systems that move products from factory to customer — bridging sales platforms with the operational infrastructure that keeps Apple running at scale and ensuring Apple's technology and business priorities move in lockstep. Description At Apple, we don’t just build products — we craft experiences that enrich people’s daily lives. The Application Production Support (APS) & Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) team is responsible for ensuring that mission-critical enterprise systems and customer-facing cloud services operate with high availability, resilience, and performance at massive scale. Application & Build Ecosystem: Programming/debugging exposure in Java and Python, along with familiarity with Java-based build tools (Maven, Gradle). CI/CD Foundations: Basic understanding of CI/CD concepts and continuous deployment tools (e.g., Jenkins, GitHub Actions). Modern Tech Exposure: Exposure to GenAI solutions, AI models, and modern AI-assisted developer/support workflows. description: TechGrove is the Centre of Excellence for Banyan Software, based in Chennai, India. It handles truck check-in, self- service terminals (kiosks), slot and dock planning, and real-time monitoring for industrial customers. We are moving flow from a single-tenant setup (WildFly, Oracle, one AWS account per customer, Elastic Beanstalk) to a cloud-native, multi-tenant platform: flow6, a multi-tenant flow API (Spring Boot, JDK 21) that serves many customers from one deployment, with strict tenant isolation flow-dynamic-ui, a configuration-driven frontend where pages, queries and forms are data, not code flow-terminal-service, the backend and configurator for our check-in kiosks An analytics and real-time layer: CDC from Postgres and Oracle into Apache Doris, Kafka (MSK), and live push to the UI much of our engineering runs through AI agents in Claude Code. Each agent has a written contract, hard rules and its own tools. Our infrastructure agents are DiVa, who works inside a workload account (EKS clusters, Dockerfiles, CI, GitOps deploys, image scans), and Otto, who works across the AWS Organization (accounts, SSO, shared networking, guardrails). They already do real work. They need a human principal who owns them. This role is that owner. You will run our platform end to end and set up what is still missing, with the agents doing much of the hands-on work under your direction. You will also keep making the agents better: safer, more capable, and more useful to the rest of the team. What you will do Own the platform Run our AWS estate: an AWS Organization with shared Networking, Monitoring and Shared Services accounts, plus customer workload accounts. EKS clusters (one per customer and environment, services as namespaces), ECR, RDS, MSK, Route 53. Own the deploy path end to end: GitLab CI from one standard template, then image build and scan, then a GitOps repo, then ArgoCD on EKS. Take new services to QA and then to production. Today that means flow6-mt, flow-dynamic-ui, the auth service and Keycloak. Make flow6 safe to run as several pods behind one service: per-tenant Quartz schedulers, database locking, cache invalidation across pods, and health and readiness probes. Set up what is missing Production secrets: External Secrets Operator with SSM Parameter Store and pod-level IAM roles (IRSA / Pod Identity), in place of hand-made Kubernetes Secrets. Identity: Keycloak for staff, the existing auth service for customers, and service accounts for system-to- system calls. Observability across accounts with Grafana, Prometheus and Loki. Alarms that are tuned, not noisy. The data platform: Apache Doris, CDC pipelines (Postgres logical replication, Oracle LogMiner), Kafka. Repeatable customer onboarding: account, SSO, VPC, monitoring. Cost governance and a clear view of what runs where and what it costs. Lead the infrastructure agents Own DiVa's and Otto's contracts: their scope, hard rules, process steps and handoffs to the other agents. Turn repeated manual work into skills: small, deterministic Python tools with read-only doctor / list / plan verbs and gated mutating verbs. Examples are Helm releases, kubectl apply, registry cleanup, and an AWS Organization skill. Keep and strengthen the safety rails: agents never delete, every change needs an up-front confirm that states cost and blast radius, guard hooks block destructive commands, and nothing goes to main without review. Check that agent output is correct. Read what they produce, test it against real systems, and fix the contract when an agent is wrong. Record decisions as Target Architecture Decisions (TADs) and keep the shared memory accurate and sourced. Be the principal Make infrastructure decisions on your own and write them down so others can follow. Work with the architects, backend and frontend developers, QA, and our Cloud Ops lead, who runs the existing customer environments. Mentor colleagues who are new to Kubernetes or to working with agents. What you bring Senior to principal-level experience in DevOps, SRE or platform engineering, including running production systems. AWS in depth: EKS, IAM (including cross-account roles and SSO / Identity Center), VPC design (including shared VPCs, RAM, peering and endpoints), ECR, RDS, Secrets Manager / SSM. Kubernetes in production: Helm or Kustomize, GitOps with ArgoCD, add-ons, network setup, rolling deploys. CI/CD: GitLab CI preferred, including self-hosted runners. Container builds with multi-stage Dockerfiles, BuildKit and image scanning (Amazon Inspector). The JVM in containers: Spring Boot services, Gradle / Maven builds, Artifactory. Databases from an operator's view: Postgres and Oracle; connection pools, migrations (Liquibase), password rotation. Scripting: Python and Bash, written to be clear, repeatable and safe. Hands-on work with AI coding agents (Claude Code or similar), or a strong wish to start. You treat an agent as a capable colleague whose work you check, not as a black box. Safety by default: least privilege, no secrets in repos or images, confirm before you mutate, and an understanding of what an SCP or a delete can break. Clear written English. German is a strong plus: many of our customers and colleagues work in German. Nice to have Multi-tenant SaaS platforms: tenant isolation, per-tenant data sources, "no tenant, no service" designs. Kafka / MSK, Apache Doris or another OLAP engine, Debezium or other CDC tooling. Keycloak and OAuth2 / OIDC. Grafana, Prometheus and Loki across several AWS accounts. Moving legacy Java EE (WildFly) workloads to containers. Proxmox / LXC or other on-prem CI infrastructure. Writing prompts, agent contracts, or evaluation suites for LLM agents. Your first 90 days 1. Weeks 1–4: Learn the estate and the agents. Run DiVa and Otto on real tasks. Write down where their contracts are thin or wrong, and fix the first gaps. 2. Weeks 5–8: Finish the QA rollout of the new stack (flow6-mt, flow-dynamic-ui, auth service, Keycloak hardening). Put production secrets handling (ESO + SSM + IRSA) in place. 3. Weeks 9–12: Agree a production readiness plan for multi-pod flow6 and the first production cluster with the team. Ship at least one new DiVa skill that removes a manual step from that path.
